title: Failure mode classification and guardrail definitions for shadow appraisal results
objective: Analyze the 13 shadow comparison reports produced by P30-T5, classify each observed failure mode into named categories, define what guardrail must exist for each category, and formally declare which failure categories are blocking versus acceptable before any live handoff of LLM appraisal authority.
exact_scope: Create one new Python module at back/app/llm/failure_taxonomy.py that defines the failure mode categories as typed constants/enums and the per-category guardrail policy as structured data. Create one new test file at back/tests/test_p30_t6_failure_taxonomy.py that validates the taxonomy structure and the blocking/acceptable classification. No changes to acceptance_rules.py, comparison_harness.py, shadow_runner.py, or any engine/settlement code.
constraints: No modifications to acceptance_rules.py, comparison_harness.py, shadow_runner.py, or prompt_schema.py
No modifications to any engine, domain model, or settlement file
No modifications to vision.md or road_map.md
The taxonomy must derive its categories from evidence in back/tests/fixtures/p30_t5_shadow_run_results.json — no invented failure modes without observed support
AppraisalSignal v1 fields remain frozen — taxonomy must not propose field changes

The blocking/acceptable determination must reference the live handoff readiness criterion: LLM output must be safe to pass to the settlement engine without producing unbounded or sign-inverted state changes
All failure mode categories must be expressed as Python enums or typed string constants, not free-form strings
acceptance_criteria: back/app/llm/failure_taxonomy.py exists and is importable with no side effects
failure_taxonomy.py defines a FailureModeCategory enum (or equivalent) with at least 4 named categories derived from observed shadow results
failure_taxonomy.py defines a BlockingClassification enum with exactly two values: BLOCKING and ACCEPTABLE
failure_taxonomy.py defines a GuardrailPolicy model (Pydantic BaseModel or dataclass) with fields: category, blocking_classification, description, and required_guardrail
failure_taxonomy.py exports a GUARDRAIL_POLICIES list containing one GuardrailPolicy entry per FailureModeCategory value
The category for LLM connection/API failure is classified ACCEPTABLE (fallback handles it deterministically)
The category for LLM parse failure (bad JSON or invalid schema) is classified ACCEPTABLE (fallback handles it deterministically)
The category for valence sign-flip (positive vs negative disagreement) is classified BLOCKING for live handoff
The category for zero-absorption override (LLM returns absorption=none when context does not support it) is classified BLOCKING
The category for semantic deviation within the same valence sign (e.g. neutral vs positive when neither is negative) is classified ACCEPTABLE with a stated guardrail
back/tests/test_p30_t6_failure_taxonomy.py exists and all tests in it pass under: cd back && python -m pytest tests/test_p30_t6_failure_taxonomy.py -v
All previously passing tests continue to pass (no regression)
required_tests: Importing failure_taxonomy causes no side effects and no network calls
Every value in FailureModeCategory has a corresponding entry in GUARDRAIL_POLICIES
No two entries in GUARDRAIL_POLICIES share the same category value
LLM connection failure category has blocking_classification = ACCEPTABLE
LLM parse failure category has blocking_classification = ACCEPTABLE
Valence sign-flip category has blocking_classification = BLOCKING
Zero-absorption override category has blocking_classification = BLOCKING
Every GuardrailPolicy has a non-empty required_guardrail string
Every GuardrailPolicy has a non-empty description string
The set of BLOCKING categories is a strict subset of all categories (not all blocking, not all acceptable)
Each entry in GUARDRAIL_POLICIES is a valid GuardrailPolicy instance (fields present and correctly typed)
non_goals: Do not implement the guardrails themselves — this task only defines and classifies them
Do not modify the comparison harness or acceptance rules to enforce the guardrails
Do not execute new LLM calls or produce new shadow run results
Do not add new fields to AppraisalOutput or AppraisalSignal
Do not propose changes to the settlement engine
Do not handle deferred ticks (T3, T5, T6, T7, T8) — scope is T1/T2/T4 only
implementation_notes: The shadow results fixture at back/tests/fixtures/p30_t5_shadow_run_results.json contains 13 reports across T1/T2/T4. Observed failure modes are: (1) LLM API/network error causing fallback — seen in T1_failure_connection_error, T2_failure_connection_error, T4_event_failure_connection_error; (2) LLM returning unparseable JSON causing fallback — seen in T1_failure_bad_json, T2_failure_bad_json, T4_no_event_failure_bad_json; (3) Multi-field semantic deviation where LLM returns enriched signal (deep/positive/high) against a neutral baseline — seen in T1_success_deep_positive; (4) Single-field valence deviation not crossing the sign boundary (neutral vs negative, neutral vs positive) — seen in T2_success_surface_negative, T4_event_success_different_valence; (5) Absorption level disagreement when no social event context is present (LLM returns surface, baseline returns none) — seen in T4_no_event_surface_structural_fail. The valence sign-flip (positive vs negative) did not appear in the T5 results but is defined by acceptance_rules.py as a severe deviation and must be classified BLOCKING in the taxonomy. The GuardrailPolicy.required_guardrail field should state the concrete enforcement mechanism required before live handoff (for example: 'sign-flip must be caught by acceptance_rules.compare and must hard-block settlement invocation', or 'fallback path must be invoked and no LLM output may reach settlement').
